title: Wife, interrupting: husband's left hand clumsy, she's sure it's a pinched nerve

turns.speaker: dispatcher
turns.text: 911, what's the address of your emergency?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: 4021 Irving, upstairs. Look, I'm probably overreacting, my husband's hand is acting up.

turns.speaker: dispatcher
turns.text: Okay, tell me what's happening with his—

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: His left hand. He keeps dropping his keys, he couldn't do his shirt buttons, and he says the hand feels clumsy and kind of fuzzy. It's that pinched nerve in his neck again, he had it last spring.

turns.speaker: dispatcher
turns.text: Is it only the hand, or the whole arm?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: The hand mostly, maybe up to the wrist. He can lift the arm. Honestly, I think he just slept on it wrong.

turns.speaker: dispatcher
turns.text: When was the last time his hand was completely normal?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: He was up on the ladder cleaning the gutters this morning, no problem. He came in about twenty past twelve and he was fine then, he made a sandwich.

turns.speaker: dispatcher
turns.text: How old is he? Any blood thinners?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Sixty-nine. He takes a cholesterol pill, nothing for the blood.

turns.speaker: dispatcher
turns.text: Okay. I'm sending help to check him. Keep him sitting down.
